subject: Vendor privacy & transfer playbook — KioskBank initial asks
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@kioskbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure.ops@kioskbank.com>, KioskBank Security <security@kioskbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Vendor privacy baseline & transfer questions for Redwood

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking a first look at KioskBank as a potential Redwood customer — I'm Amanda, head of Vendor Risk at KioskBank. We're starting vendor work for a proof-of-concept (conversational assistant for account inquiries) and need to understand how Redwood handles regulated vertical requirements before we can progress to procurement.

High-level asks:
- Can you share your standard DPA / BAA / GLBA addendum templates?
- Subprocessor inventory and planned geographic transfer paths (we have EU customers and some cross-border reporting obligations).
- Confirmation of whether Redwood Hosted processing ever stores or routes raw account identifiers (we consider that GLBA-sensitive).
- SOC 2 report or equivalent evidence and last penetration test summary.

I've attached a short vendor questionnaire (vendor_requirements.xlsx) with our priority items. We are aiming to get a baseline answer within two weeks so procurement can open an SOW. Can we schedule a 30-minute call next week with product/security?

Thanks,
Amanda Li
Head of Vendor Risk — KioskBank
[a] vendor_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@kioskbank.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure.ops@kioskbank.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor privacy baseline & transfer questions for Redwood

Amanda — great to meet you and thanks for the clear asks. I'm copying Laura (Head of Legal) to help with the DPA/BAA/GLBA pieces and Karthik on technical transfer paths.

Quick answers up front: we have public DPA and HIPAA (BAA) templates — attaching the latest internal draft for your review (redwood_dpa_v3.2.pdf). Key notes:
- Hosted API: default model for trial; we do not persist user-level raw audio files or call recordings unless customers enable them. KV caches are ephemeral but may be written to cloud storage for autoscaling (configurable).
- Subprocessors: attached inventory CSV outlines current infra, orchestration, and telemetry vendors (subprocessor_inventory_20261114.csv). We can provide attestations and subprocessors’ jurisdiction info per row.
- Cross-border: we support routing policies by region and can pin customers to Dedicated or Private deployments when residency is required. See transfer_diagram_v2.png for a high-level path mapping.

Let's do a focused 30-minute sync — I can do Tuesday 11/17 11:00–11:30 PT or Wednesday 11/18 15:00–15:30 PT. I'll include Karthik for the tech run-through and Laura for contract questions.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.2.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20261114.csv, transfer_diagram_v2.png

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@kioskbank.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure.ops@kioskbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor privacy baseline & transfer questions for Redwood

Amanda / team —

Following up with a few contract-level clarifications after Evelyn's overview. We reviewed your questionnaire and flagged the items most likely to need a tailored addendum for GLBA/HIPAA:

1) Data classification & scope: please confirm the exact data elements you expect Redwood to process (account numbers, SSNs, transaction metadata, PII, health-related notes if any). The scope will determine whether a BAA or GLBA addendum is applicable in full.
2) Data residency: for EU customer data that is personal data, we recommend either Dedicated in AWS eu-west-1 or a private deployment. If you require contractual guarantees on transfer mechanisms we can add the SCCs/standard contractual clauses or an EU-US transfer annex.
3) Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; we can provide the latest summary and a SOC bridge letter. Pen test summary (redacted) can be shared.

We typically propose the following next steps timeline:
- This week: confirm scope of data elements and residency requirements (Amanda)
- Next week: Redlines to DPA/BAA (Laura) + provide SOC 2 summary (Redwood)
- 2 weeks: procurement paperwork and initial security questionnaire completion (KioskBank)

Open questions for you: is KioskBank able to accept a provider-hosted encryption key for Hosted API or do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? That will change the recommended deployment path.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@kioskbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure.ops@kioskbank.com>, KioskBank Security <security@kioskbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor privacy baseline & transfer questions for Redwood

Thanks, Evelyn and Laura. Quick clarifications from our side after internal review:
- Scope: PII + account identifiers + transaction metadata. No PHI for this POC, but roadmap may include health-related benefits routing in 2027 — please note.
- Residency: EU personal data must remain in EU for a subset of customers; U.S. account identifiers are GLBA-sensitive.
- Keys: procurement prefers customer-managed keys (KMS) for production, but is okay with provider-hosted keys for early-stage POC.

Outstanding asks we need to close before signing SOW:
1) A redline showing the BAA/GLBA carve (if both apply) — are you able to produce a combined addendum or will you provide separate templates?
2) SOC 2 Type II summary under NDA + pen test executive summary.
3) A short note confirming that Hosted API will not route EU-personal-data through US regions when regional routing is pinned to eu-west-1.

We also prefer a checklist-style mutual action plan with owners and dates to move this into procurement. Can you send that after your internal alignment?

Amanda
Amanda Li
Head of Vendor Risk — KioskBank
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@kioskbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, ProcureOps <procure.ops@kioskbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor privacy & transfer playbook — KioskBank initial asks

Amanda — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a single combined addendum approach proposal (we can offer a combined GLBA+BAA annex or separate ones per your preference). Key points below and owners/dates in the attached MAP:

Summary answers:
- Combined addendum: we will draft a GLBA+HIPAA annex that maps to the DPA controls; Laura will produce a redline by 2026-12-06.
- SOC 2 / pentest: we will provide the SOC 2 Type II summary under NDA and the redacted pen test executive summary by 2026-12-03.
- Residual routing guarantee: for the POC we will pin processing for the EU subset to eu-west-1 and confirm that no EU-personal-data will be egressed to US regions. Karthik will provide a short technical attestation by 2026-12-01.
- Keys: POC = provider-hosted; production = customer-managed KMS (we will document the KMS onboarding steps and timing).

Next immediate step: Laura will send the DPA redline and the combined addendum proposal; Karthik will prepare the technical transfer attestation. I will schedule a 30-minute MAP review Thursday 12/01 09:00–09:30 PT.

Attachments: MAP_KioskBank_20261129.pdf (action plan table), combined_addendum_proposal_draft.docx

If you prefer a recorded walkthrough for procurement, we can record the session and drop the recording in the Drive link.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[attachment: MAP_KioskBank_20261129.pdf (PDF)]
